From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Fatima Noor <fatima.noor@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, Feb 10, 2025 at 5:42 PM
Subject: Doc review: Private Observability Minimum Pack — install guide + day-2 runbook (drafts)

Hi all —

We have first drafts for the operator-facing docs for the “Private observability minimum pack” (VPC + on-prem). Requesting review from SRE/Security/Solutions/Standards on accuracy + “supported” criteria before we convert these into the Confluence canonical pages.

Drafts:
1) Install guide (draft): Private Observability Min Pack - Install Guide (Google Doc link)
2) Day-2 runbook (draft): Observability Pack Day-2 Ops Runbook (Google Doc link)

What I’d like reviewers to focus on:
- SRE (Sean): SLO language + burn-rate alerting guidance, severity mapping, and what we promise as “page-worthy” vs ticket.
- Security (Naomi/Marcus): secure defaults (Grafana auth, TLS, RBAC), audit log expectations around dashboard/rule changes, and any “do not recommend” configs.
- Solutions/Deployments (Markus/Fatima/Bruno): install reality checks (VPC + on-prem/air-gap), common failure modes, and validation steps.
- Standards (Allison): signals/metric semantics wording, cardinality warnings, and anything that will drift from the minimum signals standard.

Timing: please add comments by EOD Wed (2/12). If anything is a blocker for the GA bundle, flag it in-thread and we’ll triage.

References we’re trying to bake in:
- SUP-2419: “no clear latency dashboards”
- SUP-2431: “rule load failures after upgrade”

Thanks,
Elliot

—
Elliot Price
Docs Lead, Redwood Inference



From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Fatima Noor <fatima.noor@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Kira Thompson <kira.thompson@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Bruno Silva <bruno.silva@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 11, 2025 at 9:14 AM
Subject: Re: Doc review: Private Observability Minimum Pack — install guide + day-2 runbook (drafts)

Left comments in both docs.

Top items:
1) Install guide should be explicit that we expect burn-rate alerting (multi-window) for availability + latency, not static thresholds. In the draft you have “p99 latency > X for Y minutes” as an example — I’d either remove or label it “last resort / customer-specific”.
2) Paging policy: recommend a default that pages only on:
   - SLO fast-burn (e.g., 2%/5m + 5%/30m) for availability
   - “No metrics / rules not loading” pipeline health (but only if sustained > 10m)
   - “Gateway 5xx spike” if above a meaningful volume threshold (to avoid low-traffic noise)
Everything else should be ticket/sev4 by default.
3) Add a callout on “rule load failures after upgrade” (SUP-2431). Suggested operator check: promtool check rules output and Prometheus UI /rules page + alertmanager config reload events.

Also: please add a short section on silencing during planned maintenance + how to do it without masking pipeline failures.

— Sean



From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Fatima Noor <fatima.noor@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Kira Thompson <kira.thompson@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Bruno Silva <bruno.silva@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 11, 2025 at 11:03 AM
Subject: Re: Doc review: Private Observability Minimum Pack — install guide + day-2 runbook (drafts)

Reviewed; comments in-line.

Security-specific changes requested:
- Grafana auth: default language should be “customer-managed IdP via OIDC/SAML (preferred), local admin only for break-glass”. Current draft reads like local admin is normal.
- TLS: the guide should assume TLS on Grafana/Prometheus endpoints, and explicitly say we do not support plaintext auth tokens over HTTP.
- RBAC: spell out least-privilege service accounts (Grafana provisioning vs read-only dashboards vs rule writers). We’ve had internal installs fail due to over-restrictive cluster roles, but we also don’t want cluster-admin as the “fix”.
- Audit logging: need a short “what we can provide” vs “what customer must enable”. Example: Grafana has its own audit logs and we recommend enabling them; Redwood components will emit audit events for API access separately.

Also, please avoid recommending storing any credentials in values.yaml examples (even “example” creds). Use placeholders and reference K8s Secrets.

Naomi

—
Naomi Feldman
Security & Compliance Product Lead
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, Feb 11, 2025 at 1:37 PM
Subject: Re: Doc review: Private Observability Minimum Pack — install guide + day-2 runbook (drafts)

Added comments from Solutions POV.

Big asks:
- Put the “validation checklist” earlier. In practice operators want a single command / checklist before they start customizing.
  *Recommend: after install steps, add “Run: redwood-private validate observability --export report.json” (or whatever Bruno lands) + what “PASS” looks like.
- “Common pitfalls” section should include:
  - ServiceMonitor not selected due to label mismatch
  - NetworkPolicy blocking Prometheus -> targets
  - Customer SIEM endpoint rejects due to mTLS/cipher mismatch
  - Grafana provisioned but dashboards empty because datasource name mismatch
- For support readiness, include a “what to collect before escalating to Redwood” list (kubectl output, prom logs, Grafana provisioning logs, alert rules list).

Related: SUP-2419 pain was that we didn’t tell them which latency panels matter (prefill vs decode, queue). The dashboard tour in the runbook should be more opinionated.

Markus

—
Markus Klein
Solutions / Pro Services Lead (Private)
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, Feb 11, 2025 at 4:22 PM
Subject: Re: Doc review: Private Observability Minimum Pack — install guide + day-2 runbook (drafts)

Commented on on-prem / air-gapped parts.

Specific gaps:
- We need to explicitly list the artifacts that must be mirrored offline (images + charts + dashboard JSONs + rules). Operators always miss the dashboard JSON bundle.
- Add a “no egress” note for time sync: if the cluster can’t reach NTP, timestamps drift and dashboards look broken. (Happened in our lab.)
- SIEM/log forwarding: clarify which targets are supported out of the box vs “customer managed”. The doc currently implies we ship a full SIEM integration.

Also, can we add a short “minimal footprint mode” note (single Prometheus, single Grafana, local storage) vs HA mode? I know the reference arch will cover it, but operators ask in the install guide.

Fatima

—
Fatima Noor
On-Prem / Air-Gapped Packaging SME
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, Feb 12, 2025 at 10:18 AM
Subject: Re: Doc review: Private Observability Minimum Pack — install guide + day-2 runbook (drafts)

Added standards comments.

Two main things:
1) Please don’t describe tenant/model/route labels as “always safe to turn on”. We should include a cardinality warning and point to the defaults (drop/limit lists). If we’re going to mention “per-tenant dashboarding”, we need to also say “only for approved label sets”.
2) Clarify the definition of “supported signals” vs “nice-to-have”. I suggested language: supported = minimal required metrics/logs present + pipeline healthy + rule groups loaded. Anything beyond that is optional.

Also, in the runbook, the “missing metrics” triage should start with “is the scrape working?” before “is the app emitting metrics?”. Otherwise we send people down the wrong rabbit hole.

Allison

—
Allison Grant
Observability Standards Lead
Redwood Inference

Recommendation on IA:
- Install guide should be “do these steps; validate; stop”. Keep it crisp.

- “minimum pack” vs “min pack” vs “baseline bundle”

Subject: Re: Doc review: Private Observability Minimum Pack — install guide + day-2 runbook (drafts)

Thanks all — super helpful.

I’ve pulled the feedback into a set of doc edits + a few “needs eng confirmation” items. Summary below so we’re aligned.

Edits I’m making in docs (no eng dependency):
- SRE: remove static latency threshold examples as defaults; replace with burn-rate guidance + “static thresholds are customer-specific” note.
- Add “silencing for planned maintenance” section without masking pipeline health.
- Security: switch language to OIDC/SAML preferred, local admin break-glass only; add TLS assumptions and “no plaintext tokens” statement.
- Add least-privilege RBAC table (provisioner vs viewer vs rule writer).
- Add “audit logging expectations” section (Grafana audit logs + Redwood audit events, what customer must enable).
- Solutions: move validation checklist earlier; add “what to collect before escalating” packet.
- Add “common pitfalls” list (ServiceMonitor label mismatch, NetworkPolicy scrape blocks, datasource mismatch, SIEM mTLS issues).
- Standards: add cardinality warning + “approved label sets” note; rewrite missing metrics triage flow to start with scrape health.
- IA/term standardization per Kira.

Items I need quick confirmation on (Bruno/Marcus/Dev):
1) Final name/syntax for the validation command (ENG-2852). I’ll use placeholders until we have it.
2) Exact default severities for:
   - “rules not loading”
   - “no metrics ingested”
   - “gateway 5xx spike”
Sean — if you can reply with the recommended defaults, I’ll bake them into the severity table.

Next steps:
- I’ll roll edits tonight/tomorrow AM and share updated links for a final skim.
- Goal is to convert to Confluence canonical pages by Mon (2/17) for the release train.

Elliot



From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Fatima Noor <fatima.noor@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Kira Thompson <kira.thompson@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Bruno Silva <bruno.silva@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 14, 2025 at 9:18 AM
Subject: Re: Doc review: Private Observability Minimum Pack — install guide + day-2 runbook (drafts)

Severity defaults I’d suggest (for the doc table):
- Rules not loading / prom rule parse errors: Sev2 (page) if sustained 10m in prod; Sev3 (ticket) otherwise.
- No metrics ingested (pipeline down): Sev2 (page) if sustained 10m AND expected traffic > minimal threshold; else Sev3.
- Gateway 5xx spike: Sev2 only if both rate + volume thresholds exceeded (avoid paging on low traffic); otherwise Sev3.

And yes: strongly recommend burn rate for availability + latency SLOs as the “primary” paging signals.

Sean
